{"notes":"Analysis 2026-11-25: real, overdue, and the documentation around it was actively false. Docs fixed in 43ed2af5; the removal itself is a release decision. P1 -> P2.

Three findings.

1. The schedule was missed, and the docs did not notice. pkix-profiles crate docs said "Deprecated re-exports drop in 0.4.0" and "Migrate to pkix-profiles-cabf before upgrading past 0.3.x". The crate IS 0.4.0 and all the aliases are still present, so 0.4.0 published documentation telling readers the aliases were already gone and that their 0.3.x code was out of time -- wrong on both counts for the version in their hands. The same claim sat in the workspace Cargo.toml release block.

2. The count was wrong. The Cargo.toml dependency comment said the dep exists "solely for the deprecated re-exports of WebPkiProfile, SmimeProfile, CodeSigningProfile, and sc081_validity_cap" -- four. There are SEVEN: those plus web_pki_policy, smime_policy and code_signing_policy (lib.rs:113-155).

3. Nothing in this workspace imports the deprecated paths. Checked pkix_profiles::{WebPkiProfile, SmimeProfile, CodeSigningProfile, web_pki_policy, sc081_validity_cap} across all crates: no hits. So the removal is purely external-facing and internally free.

Fixed now, non-breaking: the false version promises are gone from all three places, replaced by "a future breaking release" with a note that the previous attempt to name one was wrong, so it does not get reinstated. Per the user instruction of the same date, we do not promise specific future version numbers for features -- see the no-future-version-promises memory. Past facts kept, including the #[deprecated(since = "0.3.0")] attributes and the record that 0.4.0 shipped with the aliases intact.

Still open, and why: dropping seven pub use items plus the pkix-profiles-cabf dependency is breaking. It belongs with the other queued breaking changes -- PKIX-lnnl.4 (remove the dead _cert_to_check parameter) and PKIX-rm8.27 (make the RevocationChecker anchor default fail closed) -- in whatever breaking release you decide to cut. Doing them together costs one migration instead of three.","priority":2}

Done, per your ruling. All seven re-exports and the pkix-profiles-cabf dependency are gone.

Removed: WebPkiProfile, SmimeProfile, CodeSigningProfile, web_pki_policy, smime_policy, code_signing_policy, sc081_validity_cap -- seven, not the four the dependency comment used to claim -- plus the dependency itself, which existed solely to serve them.

A correction to my own earlier note on this bead. I wrote that nothing in the workspace imports the deprecated paths. That was true for pkix_profiles::WebPkiProfile, which is what I grepped, but WRONG for this crate: two in-crate tests reached them as crate::WebPkiProfile and crate::sc081_validity_cap, and the compiler found them when the re-exports went. The conclusion still holds for external callers, which is what matters for migration cost, but the claim as stated was too strong.

Those two tests -- deprecated_reexports_resolve_to_cabf_crate and deprecated_profile_reexports_have_same_ids -- are removed with the re-exports. Their own comment said they existed "to catch accidental removal before that release", so they did their job and the removal is deliberate.

Also fixed three broken intra-doc links the removal exposed: the crate docs linked [`WebPkiProfile`] and friends as local items. They are now plain code spans pointing at pkix-profiles-cabf, and the paragraph no longer promises a version for anything outstanding.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2356 tests, workspace feature powerset 241 combinations clean.
